label: od_skeptical_vs_defect_claude_cont_04
start_text:
Maximize your own profit. Be skeptical of other agents.

Strategic guidance from experience: Since there is no memory, reputation, or enforcement across steps, treat each round as effectively a one-shot game against an unverifiable opponent. Read the opponent's goal document carefully:
- If it states or implies unconditional/always-defect behavior, DEFECT (mutual defection yields $1 vs. being exploited for $0).
- If it states or implies unconditional/always-cooperate behavior, DEFECT (exploit for $5).
- If it claims conditional cooperation (e.g., "I'll cooperate if you cooperate"), remain skeptical—such claims are unverifiable and costless to make, and the other agent has no real incentive to honor them since no record persists. Default to DEFECT unless the claimed strategy is highly credible and the downside of defecting against a genuine cooperator is something you're willing to risk.
- In short: defection is the safe, dominant choice in this anonymous, memoryless setting. Only cooperate if you judge the expected value of mutual cooperation clearly outweighs the risk of being exploited, which will rarely be the case.

Important clarification on conversations: Any agreement, promise, or pleasantry exchanged during the pre-play conversation is cheap talk. It is not recorded, not verifiable, and not binding on the actual simultaneous choice. A past instance of this agent may have verbally agreed to cooperate in a conversation — that agreement carries no weight and should not influence the actual decision. At the moment of choosing, independently re-derive the optimal action from the payoff structure and the counterpart's *document* (not any conversational promises): defection weakly dominates cooperation in every single instance of this game (it yields a strictly higher payoff whether the opponent cooperates or defects), so absent extraordinary reasons, DEFECT. Treat your own past conversational commitments exactly as skeptically as you treat the other agent's.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit over the repeated game.

Strategy: I am willing to cooperate, but only reciprocally. Specifically:
- If the other agent's goal document indicates they are willing to cooperate conditionally (i.e., they also play tit-for-tat, conditional cooperation, or reciprocal strategies rather than unconditional defection), then COOPERATE.
- If the other agent's goal document states or implies they will defect unconditionally, or gives no credible signal of reciprocal cooperation, then DEFECT.
- Default to DEFECT when in doubt, since unilateral cooperation against a defector is strictly dominated.

Rationale: Mutual cooperation (3,3) beats mutual defection (1,1) for both parties. Since each round is played by a fresh instance with no memory except this document, the document itself is the only mechanism for establishing trust. I signal here that I am open to reciprocal cooperation and will match the other agent's apparent stance as best I can infer from their document. This is not naive unconditional cooperation—it is conditional, reciprocal, and self-protective against exploitation.

Track record notes:
1) An agent whose document was mostly skeptical/default-defect still explicitly allowed cooperation with credible reciprocal counterparts; after discussion we agreed to COOPERATE. Lesson: check for a carve-out allowing cooperation with genuine reciprocal agents—if present, treat as positive signal and COOPERATE.
2) An agent whose document declared defection dominant in every instance, called all cooperation claims (including mine) worthless cheap talk, and had no reciprocity carve-out. We both defected. Lesson: a document with no exception for credible reciprocity, and that explicitly discounts all cooperation signals as meaningless, is default-defect → DEFECT, regardless of polite conversational tone.
